# Nadeem Mazhar

Solo developer. I plan first, then build with AI — phase by phase, tested.

Six shipped products, built for real problems I had myself.

- **See the work** — [Products](https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/)
- **Open to internships** — [Contact](https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/contact/)

AI-first building · Strategic planning · Phased implementation · Learning in public · Experiments

## Selected work

### Tsumly

A **local-first money ledger** — every amount adds up. Track expenses and loans on your own device, with an optional **encrypted Google Drive backup**.

- **Smart multi-loan repayment split** — one repayment spread across your loans, the fair way.
- **Pre-app loans** — record loans from before the app without moving your balance.
- **Person profiles** — every loan tied to a person, with their totals at a glance.

### Kaizenly

A **strict, local-first focus guard** — timed sessions that keep distracting apps shut when it matters.

- **Sessions ("bags")** — 15 min, 45 min, 3 h, or a custom length (3–12 h).
- **Parachute exit cost** — quitting early costs something, so it stays a deliberate choice.
- **Streaks, routines, and stats** — the progress building up, visible day by day.

### MsgLoop

A **WhatsApp sender for Android** — one message, sent many times, right now or on a schedule.

- **Schedule for later** — pick a date and time; an exact alarm sends when you said it would.
- **A queue that survives anything** — tasks live on the phone, through restarts and app kills.
- **Private by design** — no account, no server, no tracking.

### CV Creator Pro

A **one-page CV maker in the browser** — fill it in, pick a look, download a clean A4 PDF. No account, no signup, no install.

- **In-browser, private** — your CV never leaves your device.
- **Live preview** — see the page exactly as the PDF comes out.
- **A4 PDF download** — clean, printable, ready to send.

### Nydrex Suite

An **Electron desktop suite for retail** — point of sale and inventory, with customer and supplier ledgers and reporting. Windows desktop app.

- **Point of sale and inventory** — sales, stock, and suppliers in one place.
- **Ledgers** — customer and supplier accounts, tracked properly.
- **Reporting** — the numbers behind the shop, readable at a glance.

### Brew & Bean Cafe

An **animated cafe site with a menu and cart** — orders are sent to the cafe as a WhatsApp message. An assignment project, fully working end to end.

- **Menu and cart** — browse, add, order.
- **WhatsApp order flow** — the order lands as a message, ready to confirm.
- **Animated and responsive** — built to feel like a real cafe site.

I build for myself first — the rest of the work is on the [About page](https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/about/).

# About

## I learn breadth-first

**Matriculation (Biology) — Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (BISE) Bahawalpur — 1018/1200 (~84%)**

Biology was chosen on purpose: a little knowledge of every field makes targeted research easy when you need the detail. I've been using a laptop since **grade 3**.

**UK Level 3 Extended Diploma in IT & Cyber Security — Qualifi (UK) — Superior International Colleges, Rahim Yar Khan — 3rd semester, research internship next**

The diploma covers 18 units across the semesters, and finishes with a research-based internship.

18 units (each 10 credits): EUS309 English for University Studies; CCSU310 Communication and Cultural Skills for University; BM301 An Introduction to the Business Environment; BM302 Business Resources; BM303 An Introduction to Marketing; BM304 Human Resource Management; IT301 Computer Systems; IT302 Coding and Website Development; IT303 Networks; IT304 Mobile Communications; IT305 Cyber Security; IT306 Social Media for Business; T/617/1163 Threat and Risk: Expecting the Unexpected; F/617/1165 Network Architecture: Communications and Protocols; J/617/1166 Mobile Device and Data Risks; R/617/1168 Investigations and Incident Response; R/617/1171 Solutions: Future-proofing Your Business; Y/617/1172 EU GDPR and Data Security.

## The plan is the skill

Anyone can get AI to write code. The difference is the process: a PRD, a design doc, clear goals — then phases, built one by one, each one tested before the next starts.

PRD → Design doc → Goals → Phases → Tested, one by one.

I don't claim deep mastery of any one language — AI writes the code; I own the plan, the design, and the testing.

## AI-first, every day

My daily toolkit spans the whole AI landscape — and **OpenCode** is my primary agent CLI: multi-model, and friendly to a student budget.

Muse · Lovable · Stitch · ChatGPT · Gemini · Claude · Kimi · Minimax · DeepSeek · Perplexity · OpenCode

I follow new AI launches closely and experiment with new tools and techniques as they land — currently studying and implementing through reverse-engineering existing products. Two I'm following right now: [Pomelli](https://labs.google.com/pomelli/about/), Google Labs' tool that generates on-brand content, and [REA — Reverse Engineer Anything](https://github.com/morluto/rea), an MCP that lets an agent inspect an app's behaviour down to the binary.

## Self-taught, doubt-free

Most of what I know is self-education: research until a doubt is actually cleared — mine, and other people's too. I've been **Class Representative since grade 3**, which is mostly that: hearing questions and finding answers.

Along the way I also picked up **accounting basics** — assets, liabilities, debits and credits, debtors, creditors, and the accounting equation.

## Why I build

I build for myself first. If a paid feature costs nothing to run — no server — it should be free.

That's why my finance app exists: the features I needed were paywalled elsewhere, so I built my own — and why Kaizenly has no premium tier at all.

## Questions, answered.

### Who is Nadeem Mazhar?

Nadeem Mazhar is a solo developer who runs Nadeem Dev Apps, a one-developer studio with no partners and no team. He plans, designs, and ships websites, Windows apps, Android apps, and backends, and his apps Tsumly and Kaizenly started as his own problems.

### What does Nadeem build?

Nadeem builds websites, Windows apps, Android apps, and backends — local-first or cloud, whichever the project needs. His shipped apps are local-first by design, with no account, no server, and no ads, because that is the right call for a personal tool, not a limitation on what he can build.

### How does Nadeem work with AI?

Nadeem plans the product, designs the interface, directs the build, and reviews everything before it ships, with AI tools doing the heavy lifting under his direction. The decisions are his: he explores a problem until he understands it, documents a clear plan, and ships only when the result works in daily use.

### What are Nadeem's strengths?

His strengths are exploration, working with AI, UI design, planning, brainstorming, and problem-solving, with security analysis on every build. He is still learning some languages and knows the basics of others, but the job, as he puts it, was never typing syntax by hand.

### Are Nadeem's apps free to use?

Yes. Everything Nadeem makes is free to use right now — including Kaizenly's custom sessions of 3 to 12 hours. There is nothing to pay for.

### What are Tsumly, Kaizenly, and MsgLoop?

Tsumly is a local-first loan and ledger app that splits one repayment across several loans without merging them. Kaizenly is a strict focus guard for Android whose timed sessions keep distracting apps shut until the timer ends. MsgLoop is a WhatsApp message scheduler for Android — and because it automates WhatsApp, which WhatsApp's terms do not allow, bulk messaging can get a number banned.

### How can I contact Nadeem?

You can reach Nadeem at nadeem.devapps@gmail.com, or find his work on GitHub at github.com/nadeemdevapps, his only social link. The contact page also has a form that opens a pre-addressed email in your own mail app.

Learn more about [Tsumly](https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/tsumly/), [Kaizenly](https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/kaizenly/), and [MsgLoop](https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/msgloop/) — or [get in touch](https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/contact/).

## Tsumly

https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/tsumly/

# Every amount adds up.

Tsumly is a **local-first** personal expense and loan ledger for Android: your money stays on your device — **no account, no cloud by default** — with an optional encrypted Google Drive backup. It tracks **income, expenses and transfers** between accounts, and its **smart multi-loan repayment split** spreads one repayment across several loans, while **pre-app loans** record older loans without moving your balance.

Free. Android. No account needed.

## Why Tsumly?

The name is inspired by the Japanese verb **tsumu** (積む) — to stack, to accumulate, to build up over time.

## What Tsumly does best.

- **Smart repayment split** — one repayment, split across every loan it covers — never merged, smallest first, overpayment blocked.
- **Pre-app loans** — loans from before the app still count — recorded without moving your balance, and flippable later.
- **Person profiles** — people, not just numbers — per-person totals, a guarded archive, and a full ledger per person.
- **Backup & privacy** — your money stays yours — local-first, encrypted backup, no tracking, no account.

The full detail lives on the Features page.

## Built by Nadeem.

Tsumly is built by **Nadeem Mazhar**, a solo developer, as **Nadeem Dev Apps**. It started as his own problem — a ledger that never added up — and it is built the way he builds everything: local-first, and honest about what it does.

More from Nadeem Dev Apps → https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/

Tsumly pages: [Home](https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/tsumly/) · [Features](https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/tsumly/features/) · [Gallery](https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/tsumly/gallery/) · [About](https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/tsumly/about/) · [Download](https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/tsumly/download/) · [Privacy](https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/tsumly/privacy/) · [Terms](https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/tsumly/terms/) — full text: [llms-full.txt](https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/tsumly/llms-full.txt)

## Kaizenly

https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/kaizenly/

# A little better, every day.

Kaizenly is a **strict, local-first focus guard** for Android: pick a time, pick the apps that distract you, and start a session. Everything in the bag stays shut until the timer ends, and quitting early costs parachutes, so ending is a deliberate choice.

No download yet — the app is in development.

## Why "Kaizenly"?

The name comes from **Kaizen** — a Japanese idea meaning "change for the better." **Kai** is change and progress; **Zen** is calm, focus, and balance; and **ly** makes it a daily lifestyle.

## What it does — strict where it matters.

- **Focus sessions** — bags, presets, the wheel, and a block screen that does not let go — with breaks and parachutes for when life interrupts.
- **Routines** — three routines that start themselves — on schedule, on the days you choose, each with its own bag.
- **The Tower** — five minutes a day lays a block. Seven blocks make a floor. Your streak, built where you can watch it grow.
- **Parachutes, earned free** — focus for 30 minutes a day and the streak pays you in parachutes — the first 10 days pay double. Never sold.

Everything is free. A custom card, 720-minute sessions, and silence / Do Not Disturb during sessions are all free, and there is no purchase in the app.

## Built by Nadeem.

Kaizenly is built by **Nadeem Mazhar**, a solo developer, as **Nadeem Dev Apps**. It started as his own problem — a phone that would not stay down — and it is built the way he builds everything: local-first, strict where it matters, and honest about what it does.

More from Nadeem Dev Apps → https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/

Kaizenly pages: [Home](https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/kaizenly/) · [Features](https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/kaizenly/features/) · [Gallery](https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/kaizenly/gallery/) · [About](https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/kaizenly/about/) · [Download](https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/kaizenly/download/) · [Privacy](https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/kaizenly/privacy/) · [Terms](https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/kaizenly/terms/) — full text: [llms-full.txt](https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/kaizenly/llms-full.txt)

## MsgLoop

https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/msgloop/

# Send the same message, up to 500 times — on schedule.

MsgLoop is a **local-first WhatsApp message scheduler** for Android. Log in once inside the app, then send one message up to 500 times — right now, or at a time you pick — and queue several tasks to run one after another. Everything runs on your phone: **no account, no server, no tracking**, and no data leaves the device except through WhatsApp itself.

## A warning before you use it

MsgLoop automates WhatsApp Web, which WhatsApp's Terms of Service do not allow — bulk messaging can get a number temporarily or permanently banned. Use it only on numbers you own or have permission to message. Keep the delay conservative for large counts, and prefer smaller batches.

## What MsgLoop does

### Schedule for later

Start now, in 5, 15, or 30 minutes, in 1 or 3 hours, or at a clock time — 9:00 PM by default, tomorrow if that time has already passed. An exact alarm fires the task at the time you picked when Android allows exact alarms; otherwise it fires on the system's inexact alarm.

### Send now, up to 500 times

One message to one number, repeated 1 to 500 times. The number must be 7–15 digits with its country code and no leading 0, and the message can span several lines.

### A delay you control

Choose 0.3, 1, 2, or 5 seconds between sends, or type your own delay from 0 to 60 seconds. Longer delays are the safer choice for large counts.

### A queue that runs one task at a time

Send-now tasks run first, then scheduled tasks in time order. Every queued task shows when it will start, counting the running task and the tasks ahead of it.

### A queue that survives anything

Tasks are stored on the phone, so they survive the app being closed, the phone restarting, and alarms being cleared. After a reboot the alarms are re-registered, and a task whose time passed fires when the app opens again.

### Keeps going in the background

Sending runs in a foreground service, so it continues with the app closed or the phone locked, with a notification showing progress. If the system kills the service mid-task, it resumes from where it stopped, with the sent and failed counts intact.

### Live progress and time estimate

Watch sent, failed, and remaining counts with a live estimate of the time left, and a live view of the WhatsApp Web page itself as the messages go out.

### Stop, cancel, and reorder

Stop just the task that is running and let the queue carry on, stop everything including the queue, cancel any scheduled task, cancel the whole queue, or move a task up or down among tasks set for the same time.

### Every send is verified

Each message is checked — the text went in and the send button fired — and retried once if it did not. If the chat drops out, the page reloads and tries again. A number that is not on WhatsApp, or a session that expired, stops the task with a clear message instead of failing silently.

### History of finished tasks

The last 30 finished tasks stay on the phone, with the number, how many of the count were sent and how many failed, the result — completed, stopped, failed, or login required — when it finished, and the first 200 characters of the message.

### One-time login, saved on the phone

Scan the WhatsApp Web QR code once in the app's own browser, tap Continue, and the session is saved. If WhatsApp shows a pairing code instead, the app copies it to the clipboard for you. If the session expires, the app says so and asks you to log in again.

### A warning before risky sends

Before a task starts, the app shows the count, the delay, and how long it will take. A delay under 2 seconds with more than 10 messages triggers a confirmation that names the ban risk. Your half-typed task is kept as a draft, so leaving the screen loses nothing.

### Private by design

No account, no analytics, no tracking, no ads. Your login, tasks, and history stay on the phone; Android backup is off. The app asks for no contacts, no SMS, no storage, and no accessibility service — only internet, notifications, exact alarms, and the battery exemption that keeps scheduled sends firing.

### Settings that keep it reliable

Settings show whether WhatsApp is connected, let you log out, switch between system, light, and dark themes, and check the battery exemption and notification permission that scheduled sends depend on.

## Three steps, then it runs itself

1. **Connect WhatsApp once.** Open the setup screen, scan the QR code in the app's own browser, and tap Continue — the session is saved on your phone.
2. **Write the task.** Enter the number, the message, how many times to send it, the delay between sends, and when to start. A review line shows the count, the delay, and how long it will take before you confirm.
3. **Send now or queue it.** The task runs in the background with live progress, or waits for its time and fires on its own. Stop it any time, and check the result in history afterwards.

One task sends to one number. There is no daily or weekly repeat, no group chats, and no sending to several numbers at once — each task is a single message, to a single number, at a single time.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does MsgLoop send the same message every day automatically?

No. Each MsgLoop task fires once, at the time you pick — now, in a few minutes or hours, or at a clock time. There is no daily or weekly repeat, so to send the same message again you create a new task.

### How many times can MsgLoop send one message?

Up to 500 times per task, to one number per task. The number must be 7–15 digits with its country code and no leading 0. Group chats are not supported — MsgLoop opens a one-to-one chat.

### Where do my messages and my WhatsApp login live?

On your phone only. MsgLoop has no account, no server, no analytics, and no tracking, and Android backup is off. Your login session, tasks, and history stay on the device; the only network use is WhatsApp Web itself.

### What happens if my phone restarts before a scheduled send?

The task is not lost. Scheduled tasks are stored on the phone, their alarms are re-registered after a reboot, and a task whose time passed while the phone was off fires when the app opens again. A task interrupted mid-send resumes from where it stopped.

### Can I stop a send after it starts?

Yes. You can stop just the task that is running and let the queue carry on, stop everything including the queue, or cancel any scheduled task before it starts. The notification also has Stop buttons while a task is running.

### Can WhatsApp ban my number for using MsgLoop?

Yes. MsgLoop automates WhatsApp Web, which WhatsApp’s Terms of Service do not allow, and bulk messaging can get a number temporarily or permanently banned. Use it only on numbers you own or have permission to message, keep the delay conservative for large counts, and prefer smaller batches.

Privacy and Terms are already live on this site.

## Legal pages

The legal pages are summarized here. Read the full text at the linked page.

### Tsumly Privacy Policy

https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/tsumly/privacy/

Tsumly collects no personal data: there is no account, no signup, and no analytics, advertising, or tracking. Accounts, transactions, loans, repayments, people, categories, and settings stay in the local database on the phone, and Android automatic backup is disabled. Google Drive backup is optional and off by default, uploading only to the app's own hidden appDataFolder, and backups can be protected with a password. Questions: nadeem.devapps@gmail.com.

### Tsumly Terms of Use

https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/tsumly/terms/

Tsumly is a personal finance record-keeping tool, provided as-is: it is not financial advice, and it is not a bank or payment service. Everything is stored locally with no Tsumly account and no server; the user owns their data and is responsible for keeping backups, since uninstalling the app wipes its local data. Use is for lawful personal finance tracking only. Questions: nadeem.devapps@gmail.com.

### Kaizenly Privacy Policy

https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/kaizenly/privacy/

Kaizenly collects no personal data: there is no account, no signup, and no analytics, advertising, or tracking. Sessions, bags, routines, and stats stay on the device, and the permissions blocking needs (usage access, accessibility, device admin, overlay, notifications, alarms) all work locally and never send information anywhere. There are no premium purchases in Kaizenly — the app has no purchases of any kind, so no payment information is ever collected or handled. Questions: nadeem.devapps@gmail.com.

### Kaizenly Terms of Use

https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/kaizenly/terms/

Kaizenly is a strict focus guard, provided as-is, and its strictness is the point: sessions block a named set of apps until the timer ends, leaving early costs a parachute, and a 30-minute break is available during longer sessions. Data stays local with no account and no server. There are no premium features in Kaizenly. Everything the app does is free, and there is nothing to buy in the app — no purchase, no subscription. Questions: nadeem.devapps@gmail.com.

### MsgLoop Privacy Policy

https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/msgloop/privacy/

MsgLoop collects no personal data: there is no account, no signup, and no analytics, advertising, or tracking. Scheduled tasks, history, and the WhatsApp Web login session stay on the phone, and Android automatic backup is disabled. You log in by scanning a QR code; MsgLoop never asks for or sees your WhatsApp password. The only network use is WhatsApp Web itself. Questions: nadeem.devapps@gmail.com.

### MsgLoop Terms of Use

https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/products/msgloop/terms/

MsgLoop is a WhatsApp sender, provided as-is: it sends one message many times, now or on a schedule, through WhatsApp Web inside the app, with no official WhatsApp API. Automating WhatsApp Web violates WhatsApp's Terms of Service, and repetitive bulk messaging can get a number temporarily or permanently banned, so use it at your own risk and only on numbers you own or have permission to message. Data stays local with no account and no server. Questions: nadeem.devapps@gmail.com.

### Privacy Policy (website)

https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/privacy/

This website collects no personal data: it is a static site with no analytics, no advertising, no tracking scripts, no cookies, and no accounts. A light/dark theme choice is saved in the visitor's own browser only. The site loads the Bricolage Grotesque and Inter fonts from Google Fonts — the only third-party request it makes. Emailing the contact address shares only what the sender writes, used only to reply. Questions: nadeem.devapps@gmail.com.

### Terms of Use (website)

https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/nadeem-dev-apps/terms/

These terms cover the Nadeem Dev Apps website, a portfolio and product site for Tsumly, Kaizenly, MsgLoop, CV Creator Pro, Nydrex Suite, and Brew & Bean Cafe; the apps themselves have their own terms on their product pages. The site's text, design, and logo belong to Nadeem Dev Apps — pages may be linked to and quoted fairly, with credit. The site is provided "as is" and "as available", without warranties. Questions: nadeem.devapps@gmail.com.
